Memory.Wiki’s wedge is **cross-AI context portability**.

Single-AI memory systems — ChatGPT Memory, Claude Projects, vendor-specific memory stores — live inside one vendor’s ecosystem. They help that vendor’s own AI, but they do not naturally serve competitors.

Memory.Wiki sits outside those silos:

> **One URL. Every AI.**

A Memory.Wiki URL can be pasted into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, or any AI that can fetch a webpage. The AI receives clean markdown / digest context without needing a proprietary integration.

The structural advantage is that **giants are incentivized not to build this**:

- OpenAI will not want to build a memory layer that makes Claude better.
- Anthropic will not want to build one that makes ChatGPT better.
- Cursor, Gemini, and others have the same ecosystem tension.

So Memory.Wiki occupies the neutral layer they cannot easily own:  
**a cross-AI delivery layer for user-authored knowledge.**

Important distinction: embeddings are not sent directly to the LLM. They power search. The LLM usually receives markdown URL payloads: doc, bundle, or hub digests.

mdfy frames its RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline as "mdfy Memory." It performs retrieval using a chunked and hybrid approach (vector + BM25 hybrid). 

Here is how the process works:

*   **Embedding & Chunking:** When a document is saved, the embedding pipeline (`/api/embed/<id>`) automatically embeds the title and body for global search. It also breaks the document down into paragraph-level chunks (section-aware) for finer recall.
*   **Storage:** The vectors are stored using `pgvector` in a Postgres database across three levels: `documents.embedding`, `bundles.embedding`, and `document_chunks.embedding`.
*   **Retrieval:** AI tools can query this data via the `/recall` API or the `mdfy_search` MCP tool. Instead of relying solely on keyword matching, it uses vector similarity to perform semantic recall (e.g., finding "which docs cover X?").

To optimize costs and efficiency, mdfy uses an `embedding_source_hash` to skip re-embedding content that hasn't changed.

Based on the "How mdfy keeps your docs, bundles, and hub fresh" document, freshness works at three layers:

**1. Document body — always fresh**
- Saves write to Postgres immediately
- AI fetches see new content within ~60 seconds
- Edge cache uses `stale-while-revalidate=300` but revalidates on change
- **No user action needed**

**2. Bundle graph — manual re-analyze**
- AI-generated themes/insights are computed once and stamped with `graph_generated_at`
- Compared against member docs' `embedding_updated_at`
- If a member doc changed, bundle is marked stale
- User clicks "Re-analyze with AI" in bundle header when ready
- Manual by design — auto-rebuilding would waste tokens mid-edit

**3. Hub concept index — automatic + manual top-up**
- Every save enqueues an ontology refresh job (deduplicated)
- Fast path runs in Vercel's `after()` closure (seconds)
- Cron worker backstops failed jobs
- Guardrails: 30-min per-doc cooldown + 200-char minimum delta to avoid burning tokens on trivial edits
- "Re-analyze (N)" banner appears when `docs_touched_at > concepts_built_at`
- Clicking only re-extracts changed docs (max 50 per click), bypasses cooldown

You can also right-click a single doc → "Re-analyze concepts" to force one doc's refresh.

The design philosophy: aggressive freshness for body markdown (no click), fast-but-not-instant defaults for AI-derived metadata with explicit override available — trading some automation for cost discipline and predictability.

mdfy treats freshness differently for each layer:

| Layer | Freshness model |
|---|---|
| **Documents** | The markdown body is always the source of truth. Saves write to Postgres immediately, and AI-facing URLs reflect changes within roughly **60 seconds**. No user action needed. |
| **Bundles** | The AI-generated bundle graph—themes, insights, canvas layout—is generated once and reused. If a member document changes after `graph_generated_at`, the bundle becomes **stale**. The UI shows **“Re-analyze with AI”** so the user can refresh it intentionally. |
| **Hub concept index** | Concepts are auto-extracted on document save. A job is queued, usually runs within seconds, and a cron worker retries if needed. |

mdfy avoids over-rebuilding AI metadata for cost and predictability:

- concept extraction has a **30-minute per-doc cooldown**
- trivial edits under **200 characters** do not trigger re-extraction
- hub pages show a **“Concepts out of date”** banner when docs changed after the last concept build
- clicking **Re-analyze** refreshes only changed docs, up to **50 docs per click**, bypassing cooldown

So: document text stays fresh automatically; AI-derived bundle and hub metadata refresh automatically when reasonable, with explicit re-analysis when precision matters.
